title: Xander Schauffele hits tee shot into patron’s shopping bag at the Masters
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 Masters second round.

Xander Schauffele’s tee shot on the eighth hole at the Masters on Thursday didn’t land quite where he intended, but it gave one patron an experience she couldn’t buy.

On the par-5 hole, Schauffele’s ball sailed a little right of the fairway and landed in a woman’s shopping bag from the pro shop at Augusta National. Well, technically, the ball landed in two bags. Inside her clear shopping bag was one of the Masters’ popular tote bags, featuring a golf theme print with pink sides and straps.

Schauffele and the rules official walked over to the bag as patrons shuffled out of the way. They peeked into the tote to determine the ball’s location in the bag’s corner and placed a golf tee in the grass to mark the spot. Schauffele then handed the bag to the woman and returned to play.

“It just flew straight into the bag,” Schauffele said. “It was a great break. That bounce would’ve put me in the pine straw, and who knows if I would’ve had a shot to hit up the hill.

“So thanks to the lady on 8.”

Since the bag is considered a movable obstruction, Schauffele was given free relief to move the bag and the ball, then place the ball back on that spot without incurring a penalty stroke.

He made par on the eighth and ended the first round at 2 under par, three strokes behind co-leaders Rory McIlroy and Sam Burns.

Schauffele regarded Thursday’s oddity as part of the game.

“It’s been a while,” he said, “but, yeah, it does happen if you’ve been doing this long enough.”
